patches.value: Adjective keeps the same position as the masculine form (noun + adjective).

evidence.notes: Feminine form identical to masculine, so no ending is added and adjective placement is unchanged; source only states the form stays the same.
Order follows the rule's formation 'passive verb + de + agent'; the agent follows the preposition de after verbs of emotion or opinion.
Order follows the rule's formation 'passive verb + par + agent'; par is the default agent preposition in the passive.

patches.value: reflexive pronoun + être + past participle (+ direct object)

evidence.notes: Reflexive pronoun precedes the auxiliary; a direct object placed after the participle is what blocks agreement, so its post-participle position is the order fact.

patches.entity_key: Agreement of pronominal verbs in plus-que-parfait
patches.value: subject + reflexive pronoun + être (imparfait) + past participle

evidence.notes: Formation is s'être (imparfait) + past participle; the reflexive pronoun attaches before the auxiliary and negation wraps auxiliary + pas.

patches.value: interrogative word + verb + hyphen + subject pronoun (Comment allez-vous ?)

evidence.notes: Signal expressions use inversion with a hyphen; Ça va ? is a fixed subject + verb order. Uncertainty: only the interrogative idioms show a distinctive order.

patches.value: au cas où + subject + conditional verb

evidence.notes: Fixed conjunction au cas où is followed by a clause whose verb is present or past conditional; the conjunction precedes the subject.

patches.value: reflexive pronoun + se laisser/se faire/se voir + infinitive [+ past participle]

evidence.notes: Formation 'reflexive pronoun + verb (conjugated) [+ past participle]'; the infinitive or participle follows the conjugated semi-auxiliary, replacing the passive agent phrase.

patches.entity_key: Avoir and être are irregular in the passé simple
patches.value: subject + irregular stem (eu-/fu-) + passé simple ending

evidence.notes: Order is unchanged (subject then verb, no auxiliary); the distinctive point is the irregular stem eu-/fu- carrying the passé simple ending.

patches.value: avoir + mal + à + article + body part

evidence.notes: Formation 'avoir mal à + article + body part'; the article is obligatory before the body part, and with a following verb the pattern is avoir du mal à + infinitive.
